newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run fuel market in stalemate.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run fuel market in stalemate.

text.p: European straight-run fuel markets were still in stalemate on Thursday, with bids and offers for the promptest cargo still far apart, traders said.

Bids for Scandinavian low sulphur were around $108 a tonne fob, although buying interest was muted. The offer was still north of the $110 level, as were the putative offer levels of sellers further out.
"Numbers may still be the same but I think sellers are getting a little bit twitchy," said one trader.
Russian straight-run was flowly freely out of northern and southern ports but was principally pressuring bunker and cracked fuel markets.
A Spanish refiner was heard to have bought two cargoes of M-100 on Wednesday -- one cracked and the other straight-run -- and paid very similar numbers. No other Russian cargoes were heard traded.
